heading: Chapter 2 · It is unnatural for the People to Govern, or Chose Governours. · Argument … Section 1

items.text: Obey your father as the natural ruler of the household, for his authority is by the law of nature.
items.quote: If then the Fatherhood enjoyed this Authority for so many Ages by the Law of Nature

items.text: Submit to the eldest in the house, for he is king within the household.
items.quote: for the eldest in every house is King: And so for Kindredsake it is in Colonies.

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 3 · Positive Laws do not infringe the Natural and Fatherly Power of Kings. · Section 7 … Section 8

items.text: Obey your master when he commands you not to go to church on the Sabbath; the sin is his, not yours.
items.quote: if a Master Command his Servant not to go to Church upon a Sabbath-day, the Best Divines teach us, That the Servant must obey this Command
items.conflict: Acts 5:29: We must obey God rather than men.

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 2 · It is unnatural for the People to Govern, or Chose Governours. · Section 10 … Section 11

items.text: Govern your household as its natural head, for in every family the government of one alone is most natural.
items.quote: in every Family, the Government of One Alone, is most Natural

items.text: Submit to your father's kingly rule; the fathers of particular families bore kingly government and the elders alone swayed.
items.quote: the Elders of the Congregation bare only Sway

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 1 · That the first Kings were Fathers of Families. · Section 5 … Section 7

items.text: Obey your father as the family's ruler, for fathers are set over their families as heads and princes.
items.quote: distinct Families, which had Fathers for Rulers over them

items.text: Exercise headship and rule over your own children as their father and prince.
items.quote: the Parents were Heads and Princes.

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 2 · It is unnatural for the People to Govern, or Chose Governours. · Section 2 … Section 3

items.text: Submit to your husband, for by right of creation he has power over his wife.
items.quote: he had a power over his Wife

items.text: Do not imagine that leaving your father's house makes you free; remain under his fatherly commands even when married and having your own children.
items.quote: all that were under his Commands, were of his Family, although they had many Children or Servants married, having themselves also Children.
items.conflict: Genesis 2:24: a man leaves his father and mother and cleaves to his wife; parents retain honor, not perpetual rule over a married child's household.

items.text: Obey your master as part of his household, for he holds complete economic power over his servants.
items.quote: he might also in process of Time have Servants and a Compleat Family; and in that Family he might have compleat Oeconomical Power.

items.text: Submit to the head of the family, for he holds absolute power of life and death within his house.
items.quote: Adam and the Patriarchs had Absolute power of Life and Death, of Peace and War, and the like, within their Houses or Families
items.conflict: God alone holds absolute power over life and death; no human father or household head may lawfully kill or wage war without God's express warrant.

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 3 · Positive Laws do not infringe the Natural and Fatherly Power of Kings. · Argument … Section 1

items.text: Do your best for the preservation of your household.
items.quote: every Father is bound by the Law of Nature to do his best for the preservation of his Family

items.text: Submit to your father's government; bring no action or remedy against it.
items.quote: There is no Nation that allows Children any Action or Remedy for being unjustly Governed
items.conflict: Denies children legal protection from unjust parental rule; conflicts with biblical justice and the duty of fathers not to provoke children.

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 1 · That the first Kings were Fathers of Families. · Section 8 … Section 10

items.text: Let your desire be subject to your elder brother, and accept his rule over you.
items.quote: His Desires shall be subject unto thee, and thou shalt rule over him.
items.conflict: No brother has natural lordship over another; all are under parents and God.

items.text: Bow to the brother who holds the father's birthright and be subject to him as lord over his brethren.
items.quote: Be Lord over thy Brethren, and let the Sons of thy Mother bow before thee.
items.conflict: Christ forbids lording it over one another; no brother inherits fatherly authority.

items.text: Honor your father and mother, and render them the obedience due by natural law.
items.quote: If Obedience to Parents be immediately due by a Natural Law

items.text: Preserve, feed, clothe, instruct and defend your household; exercise a father's care over them.
items.quote: as the Father over one Family, so the King as Father over many Families extends his care to preserve, feed, cloth, instruct and defend the whole Commonwealth.

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 2 · It is unnatural for the People to Govern, or Chose Governours. · Section 4 … Section 5

items.text: Obey your father and mother in all things; do not be a disobedient son.
items.quote: many Nations have no such Custome, but on the contrary have strict Laws for the Obedience of Children

items.text: Provide for the common good of your children as well as their particular good.
items.quote: it is the Duty of a Father, to provide as well for the Common Good of his Children, as the Particular

items.text: Nourish your father in his age and need.
items.quote: Solon made a Law, which acquitted the Son from Nourishing of his Father, if his Father had taught him no Trade

items.text: Teach your son a trade so that he may earn his own living.
items.quote: if his Father had taught him no Trade, whereby to get his Living

items.text: Restrain a son who publishes seditious laws; remove him from the assembly as one under your fatherly authority.
items.quote: The Fathers have drawn out of the very Assemblies their own Sons; when being Tribunes, they have published Laws tending to Sedition

work: Patriarcha, or The Natural Power of Kings
heading: Chapter 1 · That the first Kings were Fathers of Families. · Section 2 … Section 4

items.text: Be subject to your parents, for this subjection is ordained by God.
items.quote: I see not then how the Children of Adam, or of any man else can be free from subjection to their Parents

items.text: Remain subordinate to your grandfather, the first parent, as lord over his children's children in all generations.
items.quote: but still with subordination to the First Parent, who is Lord-Paramount over his Childrens Children to all Generations
items.conflict: A man leaves his father and mother and cleaves to his wife; no grandfather holds absolute authority over all descendants (Gen 2:24).

items.text: Submit to your father-in-law's judgment, for he holds patriarchal authority over you, even in capital matters.
items.quote: Iudah the Father pronounced Sentence of Death against Thamar his Daughter-in-law, for playing the Harlot
items.conflict: The civil magistrate, not a private family head, bears the sword of capital justice (Rom 13:4).

items.text: Serve in your household head's army when he commands, as part of his family.
items.quote: Abram commanded an Army of 318 Souldiers of his own Family
items.conflict: The sword of war belongs to the civil magistrate, not a private family head (Rom 13:4).
